semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying: {نَصْرُ الله}: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in construct with its agent; its object is omitted because the meaning is understood, i.e. Allah's help to you and the believers. Likewise the objects of «الفتح» and what it is attached to: "and the opening", i.e. the opening of the lands to you and your community. Or what is intended is: "when these two acts come", without regard to what they are attached to, as in His saying: {أَمَاتَ وَأَحْيَا} [al-Najm: 44]. The al- in «الفتح» is a substitute for the construct (iḍāfa), i.e. "and His opening", according to the Kufans; according to the Basrans the referring pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, i.e. "and the opening from Him", because [the context] indicates that. What governs «إذا» is either «جاء» — this is Makkī's view, and the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] inclined to it and supported it in several places; this was given before as I transmitted it from Makkī and from him — or, second, it is «فَسَبِّحْ», to which al-Zamakhsharī and al-Ḥawfī inclined. The Shaykh rejected this from both of them on the ground that what comes after the fāʾ of the apodosis does not govern what comes before it. There is a discussion of this, part of which was given in Sūrat «والضُّحى».

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {يَدْخُلُونَ}: it is either a ḥāl (circumstantial), if «رَأَيْتَ» is visual — in al-Zamakhsharī's wording: "if it is in the sense of 'you beheld' or 'you knew (ʿarafta)'"; the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] disputed this with him, [saying] that raʾayta is not known to be in the sense of ʿarafta; he said: "So that needs verification" — or it is a second object, if it is in the sense of ʿalimta, transitive to two objects. This is the reading of the generality, I mean «يَدْخُلون» in the active. Ibn Kathīr, in one transmission, read «يُدْخَلون» in the passive. «في دين» is a figurative adverb of place, and it is an eloquent, effective figure here.
His saying: {أَفْوَاجاً}: a ḥāl from the agent of «يَدْخُلون». Makkī said: "Its analogical [plural] is afwuj, except that the ḍamma is felt heavy on the wāw, so they likened faʿl — meaning with sukūn — to faʿal — meaning with fatḥa — and gave it its plural." — end of quote. I.e. faʿl with sukūn has as its analogical [plural] afʿul, like fals and aflus, except that the ḍamma on the wāw was felt heavy, so they gave it the plural of faʿal with a vowelled middle, like jamal and ajmāl; because faʿl with sukūn [pluralised] on afʿāl is not analogical when the faʿl is sound, as in farkh and afrākh, zand and aznād — many words of this kind are attested, yet they did not make it a rule. Al-Ḥawfī said something of this.
His saying: {بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ}: a ḥāl, i.e. accompanied by His praise. The verification of this was given in al-Baqara at His saying: {وَنَحْنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِكَ} [al-Baqara: 30].
